text: Wrap (Radio w/ACT) Due Thursday 1-31 (Prior to class) 50 points Story Idea #1 - Shutdown The month-long partial government shutdown is all about a standoff over a wall. It's only about a quarter of the federal government affected by the shutdown, but some groups of workers are particularly hard hit, like the Transportation Security Administration. Focus on how the shutdown is affecting the people of Moscow and Latah County, focus on one or two areas below and talk to those working in the industries below. Travel – Moscow/Pullman airport Military – Interview someone in the ROTC program on campus, or head to the Local recruitment office in town. Taxes – Will your tax return be delayed? How are Native American Tribes affected by the shutdown? What about court cases? Can you get a marriage license? What about food safety? Financial aid for students? Story Idea #2: Sexual Misconduct Policy Changes: Why did the University revisit this policy? What was the policy prior to the change? Why is this a major concern on college campuses across the nation? What prompted the change? You will work in pairs for this assignment, but you will both write and record your own rendition of the story. You must arrange an interview and record your entire interview. Write and record a :45-1:00 radio story (a wrap) with at least one actuality. Make sure the story focuses on how the shutdown is affecting the community. Do research on all the areas above. Formulate questions (in class) to make sure your interview runs smoothly. You may use your phone to record the interview, but make sure the phone microphone is close in proximity to the mouth of your subject. You may also checkout a digital recorder from checkout with a mic. Editing software: Use any software you are comfortable with. Audacity and Final Cut are on all editing bay computers. Audacity is free and you can download on your laptop. How to write a radio story with an actuality – this is also known as a wrap. Research your topic. Write out at least six good questions for your source Conduct the interview. Consider location and make sure you find a place that is quiet. Audio clarity is important. After the interview ask yourself if you need more information. If so, reach out to another source. Remember most of this exercise is about gathering news. Will NAT sound add to your story? (NAT SOUND is sound from the location) If you are – let’s say doing a story about a coffee shop, sounds of the barista making drinks might add to your story. Only use if necessary. After you have completed your interview, write out your interview verbatim. You will use this interview to write your story. This will help you to also find the best actuality. Use only the most compelling and powerful ACT. Introduce the speaker first in the graph prior (say something) then lead into the audio cut. The graph after the actuality is also important. No wasted sentences. Please do NOT write Rep. Cathy McMorris said…. Prior to a sound bite. Complete your sentence, use that graph to give more information. Use proper format. Slow down, use pauses when necessary and try not to sound like you are reading your copy.
